title: Carnival Legend, 6 nights in the Bahamas
hook: A tight-budget, free-fun plan for the December 13 to 19 sailing from Tampa, with a day-by-day strip, port tables, and a Nassau walking sketch.

location.name: Tampa Terminal 3
location.note: Embark pin for this sailing. OpenStreetMap places Port Tampa Bay Cruise Terminal 3 at 815 Channelside Drive. The port garage is across the street at 810 Channelside. The pin is that published address, not a surveyed parcel line.

narrationScript:
This is a Beta research briefing for the Carnival Legend sailing from Tampa, December 13 to December 19, 2026. The plan is a tight budget that favors free fun. The numbers are an example, not a booked invoice.

The ship leaves Tampa Terminal 3, 815 Channelside Drive, at 3:30 in the afternoon on Sunday. Be aboard 60 minutes before sailing, which is 2:30.

Monday is a sea day. Saturday the ship is due back in Tampa at 8 in the morning.

Tuesday and Wednesday are not settled on this page. Sail From Tampa lists RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay on December 15, and Celebration Key on Grand Bahama on December 16. CruiseDen swaps those two islands. Nassau on Thursday, December 17, matches in both listings. Confirm the order in the Carnival Hub app.

RelaxAway is the free beach day. The ship docks at a new pier. Bring a towel from the ship. Lunch at the beach grills is included. The drink package does not work on the island.

Celebration Key can stay cheap if you stop after the one included Island Eats meal. The island is cashless. Leave cash on the ship and set a Sail and Sign spending cap. Bought drinks, including water and soda, are charged. The island add-on in The Carnival Cruise Blog is an 18 percent service charge plus 10 percent Bahamian VAT. That is not the ship rate. On the ship, the service charge is about 20 percent.

The Suncastle racing slides may carry a small fee per ride. Sources do not agree. Check the island or the Carnival Hub app.

In Nassau, Junkanoo Beach is a walk west. The Queen's Staircase is a walk uphill. Fort Fincastle is closed for restoration, so look from outside. The number 10 jitney toward Cable Beach is about a dollar fifty, cash only, exact change, and it passes the Arawak Cay Fish Fry. There is no Uber. Agree on the taxi price first.

The U.S. State Department advisory is Level 2, exercise increased caution, renewed July 28, 2026. Stay in the tourist core. Avoid the area called Over the Hill, south of Shirley Street. Do not swim alone. Use licensed jet ski and boat operators only.

Gratuities are 17 dollars per person per night in a standard stateroom, 102 dollars for six nights, billed to Sail and Sign. A disciplined port total in this plan is 0 to 40 dollars. Skip the drink package. Parking in the example is about 48 dollars for seven days at 717 Parking, versus about 126 dollars for six nights in the port garage.

All aboard is usually 30 minutes before departure. This plan says to be back at the pier one hour before that all-aboard call. Another note says 60 minutes before departure. Those cushions are different. Take the earlier one, and read the posted call in the Carnival Hub app.

sections.heading: The week, and the day that swaps
sections.body:
Carnival Legend sails from Tampa Terminal 3, 815 Channelside Drive, on Sunday, December 13, 2026, at 3:30 PM, and is due back Saturday, December 19, at 8:00 AM. Be aboard 60 minutes before sailing. For a 3:30 PM departure, that is 2:30 PM. The plan is a tight budget that favors free fun.

Sail From Tampa, citing Carnival, lists Monday and Friday at sea, RelaxAway at Half Moon Cay on Tuesday from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Celebration Key on Grand Bahama on Wednesday from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, and Nassau on Thursday from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM. CruiseDen lists Celebration Key on December 15 and RelaxAway on December 16. The source notes for this page also name Travel Weekly for that swap. Nassau on December 17 is the same in the listings opened here. Confirm the order in the Carnival Hub app. The strip above marks Tuesday and Wednesday so the conflict is hard to miss.

All aboard is usually 30 minutes before departure. This plan says to be back at the pier one hour before that all-aboard call. Another note in the same packet says to be back 60 minutes before departure. Those cushions are not the same. Take the earlier one, and read the posted all-aboard time in the Carnival Hub app.

sections.heading: What the money labels mean
sections.body:
Gratuities for a standard stateroom are $17 per person per night, up from $16 on April 2, 2026. Six nights is $102, billed to Sail and Sign unless they were prepaid. Suites are $19 on Carnival's page.

Keep the two service charges apart. On the ship, the rate is about 20% on drinks, drink packages, specialty dining, and spa. Carnival's gratuity page states that 20% on beverages, specialty dining, and other for-pay food, and reporting dates the rise from 18% to 20% in December 2025. At Celebration Key, The Carnival Cruise Blog reports a different add-on: 18% service charge plus 10% Bahamian VAT on island purchases. The 18% figure belongs to the island. The 20% figure belongs to the ship.

Skip the drink package. It does not work at Celebration Key or at RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay. On the ship, the plan is free water, lemonade, and tea, plus the dining room and the buffet.

The chart is an example disciplined budget, not a booked invoice: about $102 in gratuities, $0 to $40 across all three ports, and $0 in drinks because no drink spend is priced. The parking contrast sits on the Value Travel Bot strip, not in that chart.

sections.heading: RelaxAway, the free beach day
sections.body:
If Tuesday holds, this is the best $0 day. The ship docks at the new pier and you walk ashore. Cruise Radio describes a 1,005-foot pier on the north side of the island. The Points Guy describes that dock as the first on the island and large enough for two Carnival ships. Carnival's June 1, 2026 release describes the same new pier and the new tram.

Included: the beach, loungers, umbrellas, the tram, and lunch at Orchid Beach Grill or Hibiscus Beach Grill. The meal window in these notes is about 11:30 to 1:30. Cruise Radio's buffet list covers burgers, chicken, pulled pork, a nacho bar, and desserts, plus water, lemonade, and tea at the food pavilions.

Not included: sodas, alcohol, lockers at $11.99, snorkel gear starting at $21.99 on Carnival's excursion page, and, on the Eat Sleep Cruise list, a float mat at $21.99, a nature walk or bike tour at $26.99, daybeds from $149.99, and cabanas from $799.99. Towels are not handed out on the island. Bring a ship towel and return it. These notes say an unreturned towel is charged.

The drink package does not work ashore.

sections.heading: Celebration Key, free if you stop
sections.body:
Celebration Key is on Grand Bahama, and it is cashless. No cash. Leave the small bills on the ship and set a Sail and Sign spending cap before you get off. Those bills are for Nassau: the jitney and the Fish Fry.

The free shape of the day is a mile-long beach, two lagoons, chairs, umbrellas, sports courts, trams, live music at Paradise Plaza, and one Island Eats walk-up meal: an entree, fries, and a cookie. A guide that says it is following Carnival's destination guide also lists a Junkanoo parade at Paradise Plaza. The Carnival Cruise Blog describes Starfish Lagoon, Calypso Lagoon, and a large freshwater lagoon, and it says water refill stations are on the island.

After that one meal, purchases are charged, including water and soda. The blog's island add-on is 18% plus 10% Bahamian VAT. That line is only for Celebration Key.

The Suncastle racing slides may carry a small fee per ride. Sources conflict: one guide lists the tower as free, and The Carnival Cruise Blog describes a per-ride charge. Confirm on the island or in the Carnival Hub app. This page does not print a settled slide price.

Pearl Cove is the paid adults area. Guides that cite Carnival's prices list $59.99 to enter and $109.99 with open bar. Skip it, and skip cabanas, on this budget. The drink package does not work on the island.

sections.heading: Nassau on foot, then the number 10
sections.body:
Nassau is the open port. The sketch is a direction aid: west along the water to Junkanoo Beach, uphill inland to the Queen's Staircase, and the number 10 jitney west toward Cable Beach, passing Arawak Cay Fish Fry. It is not a surveyed map.

Junkanoo Beach is about a 10 to 13 minute walk west. It is crowded on cruise days. A chair, if you rent one, is about $15 in these notes. The Queen's Staircase is about a 13 minute uphill walk. The Nassau tourism board says paving reduced the old 66 Steps to 64. Cruiser Hacks also records 65 steps still described as visible. Both counts stay. Fort Fincastle at the top was still closed for restoration in a November 18, 2026 check, so the plan is the view from outside. Look again before the sail in case that changes.

The number 10 jitney is about $1.50, cash only, exact change, about 6:00 AM to 6:30 PM, and it passes the Fish Fry on the way to Cable Beach. Catch it near Frederick Street and Bay Street, a short walk from the wharf. There is no Uber.

Taxis use fixed zone fares. Agree the price before the cab moves. The 2024 New Providence zone schedule lists $12 from Prince George Dock to downtown and $20 to Cable Beach. These notes also say about $9 per cab for a short hop. Those numbers do not match, so do not treat $9 as the current table.

Skip Atlantis and ship tours.

Safety: the U.S. State Department renewed a Level 2 advisory on July 28, 2026, exercise increased caution, mainly for crime. Most of that crime note is about Nassau and Freeport. Stay in the tourist core. Avoid the Over the Hill area south of Shirley Street. Never swim alone. Use only licensed jet ski and boat operators.

sections.heading: Tampa: drive, weather, parking, debark
sections.body:
The drive from Tallahassee to Tampa is about 4 hours, I-10 east to I-75 south. These notes say there are no tolls if you skip the Selmon Expressway. Leave about 7:00 AM to be at the terminal about 11:30 AM, ahead of the 2:30 PM all-aboard.

NWS daily normals for Tampa on December 13 to 18 are a high of 74 F and a low of 56 F. December 19 is 73 F and 56 F. The December monthly normals are 73.9 F and 55.9 F. A sailaway in the mid-50s can feel chilly. Bring a light layer. This is the climate normal, not a forecast. Check the forecast closer to the sail.

Parking, labeled by length of stay so the two deals are not fake twins. Embark Day, checked October 2026, lists 717 Parking Channelside Lot at $48.23 for 7 days, fees included. That is the about $48 bar. The port garage at 810 Channelside Drive is $19 a night plus an $11.99 fee. Six nights at $19 is $114, plus $11.99, which is $125.99, the about $126 bar. Embark Day also lists that garage at $144.99 for 7 days before fees. Same garage, different length, and the fee is extra on that 7-day line. Harbor Lot is listed in these notes at about $6 a day as another cheaper off-site option. The trip notes say to prepay the garage a day ahead and that the gate does not take debit cards.

Debark on December 19 is a self-assist walk-off. Carry your own bags. Eat breakfast on the ship first. These notes put you in the car about 9:00 AM and home about 1:30 PM.

sections.heading: What to pack
sections.body:
Embark bag: passport card and driver's license, phone, charger, power bank, medications, swimwear, sandals, and a light layer. Do not put document numbers or photos of those IDs on a page like this.

Cabin: a non-surge USB cube, because these notes say surge protectors are banned, plus magnetic hooks and a refillable bottle.

Drinks you may carry on, from Carnival's rule: one sealed 750 ml bottle of wine or champagne per adult 21 or older, and up to 12 sealed non-alcoholic cans or cartons per person. Liquor and beer in luggage are confiscated. Fortified wine over 15% alcohol is outside the wine exception. A corkage fee applies if the dining room opens the bottle. This plan does not need that.

Port bag: Sail and Sign card on a lanyard, ID, reef-safe sunscreen, hat, sunglasses, water bottle, a breakfast snack, a dry pouch, the ship towel, and the phone set to ship time. Small U.S. bills are for Nassau only. On Celebration Key day, leave the cash on the ship.

Back aboard: use the earlier of the two cushions above, then follow the time posted in the Carnival Hub app.
